title: My Dad Said My Games Rotted My Math Brain #shorts

cast.kid: a stick-figure boy with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, spiky brown hair and an orange hoodie
cast.dad: a stick-figure father with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, a short black beard, square glasses and a blue plaid shirt

lines.text: Dad said my games rotted my math brain, so who was really bad at math?
lines.image: {kid} is the only person in the picture, sitting alone on a living room couch holding one game controller, looking up worried, a cozy evening living room

lines.text: My game squad has twenty-three players, and the game puts a cake on each birthday.
lines.image: {kid} is the only person in the picture, sitting on a bedroom floor holding one game controller, smiling at exactly one glowing TV screen in front of him showing two small birthday cakes, a cozy bedroom

lines.text: Two friends got cakes the same day, and I told Dad that happens a lot.
lines.image: {kid} is the only person in the picture, standing in a kitchen doorway, pointing back toward his bedroom and smiling, explaining something excitedly

lines.text: Dad laughed, still eating leftover cake from his office party, "One in three sixty-five, buddy."
lines.image: {dad} is the only person in the picture, sitting at a kitchen table eating exactly one slice of birthday cake from one paper plate, laughing, an evening kitchen

lines.text: He locked my console in his closet until I could prove it with real math.
lines.image: {dad} is the only person in the picture, putting exactly one game console onto a high closet shelf in a hallway, a stern face

lines.text: I sat alone on my floor, scared my games really had broken my brain.
lines.image: close-up of {kid} sitting alone on his bedroom floor, hugging his knees, sad eyes looking down, a single tear on his cheek, dim bedroom light

lines.text: Next day, a library book showed me a famous math puzzle called the birthday paradox.
lines.image: {kid} is the only person in the picture, sitting at a school library table reading one big open book, eyes wide with surprise, bookshelves behind him

lines.text: Dad counted one birthday, but any two people in a group can be the match.
lines.image: {kid} is the only person in the picture, standing at a classroom chalkboard drawing many small stick people joined by lines, pointing at two of them

lines.text: Twenty-three people make two hundred fifty-three pairs, so a shared birthday beats a coin flip.
lines.image: {kid} is the only person in the picture, flipping one big coin into the air in a backyard, grinning with confidence, afternoon sun

lines.text: So I asked Dad one question: why was there leftover cake from his office party?
lines.image: {kid} is the only person in the picture, standing in a kitchen with arms crossed and a sly smile, exactly one half-eaten cake on the counter beside him

lines.text: He admitted two of his twenty-three coworkers share a birthday, so they share one cake.
lines.image: {dad} is the only person in the picture, standing frozen in a kitchen holding exactly one paper plate with one cake slice, mouth wide open in shock

lines.text: Console back, and Dad still says luck, but his own office cake says math.
lines.image: {kid} is the only person in the picture, sitting on a living room couch happily holding one game controller, exactly one slice of cake on a plate beside him, cozy evening
